Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

time noun

also in time, in the course of time, in a short time, there is no time to waste, no time to lose, at the time when, in Roman times, not have the time to, time passes

classical

Cic. Att. 13.45.2: ad tempus redīre, to come back in time (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 394

tempus, temporis n.

noun, third declension

time: the time that passes, and the time for something

English “time” is several Latin words: free time is ōtium (see leisure, spare time), an age or period aetās (see age), the time of day hōra (see hour, what time is it?), an occasion tempus or aliās (see occasion), and “three times” a numeral adverb, ter. In the ablative, tempore alone means “in time, gradually”, and temperī “on time”.

Examples

  • tempore rūricolae patiēns fit taurus arātrī

    in time the bull comes to bear the farmer’s ploughOv. Tr. 4.6.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. tempus)

  • prōcēdente tempore

    in the course of timePlin. Ep. 6.31.17 (Lewis & Short s.v. prōcēdō); Traupman 394

  • in brevī spatiō

    in a short timeTraupman 394; Lewis & Short s.v. brevis

  • mātūrātō opus est

    there is no time to waste (literally “there is need of haste”)Traupman 395; cf. Liv. 24.23: quam mātūrātō opus erat (Lewis & Short s.v. mātūrō)

  • quā tempestāte

    at the time whenTraupman 394

  • aetāte Rōmānā

    in Roman timesTraupman 394

  • ōtium nōn habēre (+ dative of the gerund)

    not to have the time to (do something)Traupman 395

See also occasion, leisure, spare time, age, hour, what time is it?, on time, long, short, spend, waste time, pass the time, it’s high time, I haven’t got time, there was a time when, once, three times, temporary.
